source.title: The Cave Beneath the Sun Pyramid, Teotihuacan: Narrative of a Reverentially Terminated Mountain-Cave
source.author: Rebecca Sload

findings.subject: Painted flower-pot censer in the Sun Pyramid cave entrance
findings.assertion: In TE28's undisturbed Area D fire-pit deposit associated with radiocarbon sample Beta 220763, excavators recovered a flower-pot-type censer rim/body fragment reported to weigh 68.1 g and to bear a post-firing whitewash with fugitive cinnabar-red paint. Sload identifies it as a Tzacualli–Miccaotli or possibly Miccaotli–Early Tlamimilolpa example; the charcoal date pertains to the deposit, not directly to the manufacture of the vessel.
findings.place: Area D, cave entrance below Sun Pyramid, Teotihuacan, Mexico
findings.period: Early Teotihuacan; phase attribution debated (Tzacualli–Miccaotli or Miccaotli–Early Tlamimilolpa)
findings.evidence_type: Excavated ceramic object described in archaeological monograph; illustrated photo/drawing; contextual charcoal association
findings.inspection_status: evidence-examined (publication text and original page image)
findings.confidence: moderate that published catalog reports described object; ceramic phase and ritual significance unresolved
limitations: Cinnabar designation attributed to publication; no independent pigment analysis inspected
A cave fire-pit carbon sample does not directly date firing/painting of the vessel
Sload explicitly leaves alternative early ceramic-phase attribution open
educational_uses: Contextual sidebar: color and ceramic rituals

findings.subject: Introduced minerals in the Sun Pyramid cave terminus
findings.assertion: Sload documents magnetite fragments from a bright-yellow crushed-tepetate (BYCT) layer in TE28 Area B:West and a gypsum specimen from INAH backfill in Area B:East, illustrated in Figure 8.5. Field identification of the magnetite was followed by S. Davidovits' magnet test in the laboratory in 2009. Figure 8.5 also depicts a green stone with incised lines on its polished face. The differing contexts must be maintained: backfill specimens cannot be assigned to an undisturbed original placement.
findings.place: Area B:West and Area B:East, eastern terminus of cave beneath Sun Pyramid, Teotihuacan, Mexico
findings.period: Early cave use proposed; original placement of several pieces uncertain
findings.evidence_type: Excavated geological/stone specimens, photos and lab magnet test reported by excavation synthesis
findings.inspection_status: evidence-examined (publication text and original page image)
findings.confidence: moderate for published objects and separate stated contexts; low for intended symbolic function
limitations: Original mineral identification and specimen inventory are not independently inspected
Magnetism test is reported, not reproduced here
Ritual/numinous association is authorial interpretation, not directly demonstrable
Some specimens came from disturbed INAH backfill
educational_uses: Sun Pyramid cave mineral technology and deposition dossier
Museum object investigation into magnetite, gypsum, and greenstone

enrichments.proposed_addition: TE28's 90 undisturbed sherds in Table 8.1 comprise 33 ollas, 36 bowls, 8 jars, 9 plates/low dishes, 2 censers, and 2 with missing shape data. The 183 disturbed TE28 sherds are separate from 148 items in a 1977 surface collection; together the three collections total 421 sherds. These shape counts enrich the already existing v97-sun-06 finding without counting a duplicate canonical finding.
